issues.description: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md defines the class as 'Course' while the rest of the problem description, the template, and the solution refer to the class as 'Lecture'. This inconsistency in the class name between the specification (UML) and the provided code can confuse students about which class they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Update the UML diagram in problem_statement.md to use 'Lecture' instead of 'Course' (and ensure the UML attributes/methods remain the same), or alternatively update the textual references to match 'Course' if that is the intended name. Preferably keep 'Lecture' to match the template and solution code.

issues.description: The problem statement text and code refer to a Lecture class, but the UML diagram in the problem statement declares the class as Course. This inconsistent class name (Lecture vs Course) across the problem description and UML can confuse students mapping requirements to the provided template and solution which both use Lecture.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the class name across artifacts. Rename the UML class from Course to Lecture (or, less preferably, change textual/code references to Course). Update the problem_statement UML block so the class header reads 'class Lecture' and any references in the diagram match the Lecture attributes to avoid mismatch with the template and solution code.
